description: Dynamic Programming (DP) is an algorithmic paradigm that solves a given complex problem by breaking it down into simpler subproblems and storing the results of these subproblems to avoid computing the same results again. It is primarily used when the problem exhibits overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure.
important_details: Overlapping Subproblems: The same subproblems are solved multiple times.
Optimal Substructure: The optimal solution to the main problem can be constructed from optimal solutions of its subproblems.
Two main approaches: Top-Down (Memoization - recursion + caching) and Bottom-Up (Tabulation - iterative loop filling a table).
other_relevant_details: To identify a DP problem, look for keywords like 'maximum', 'minimum', 'number of ways', 'is it possible', or optimization tasks. The hardest part is usually defining the 'state' (what variables uniquely identify a subproblem) and writing the 'transition equation' (how one state relates to another).

variations.description: DP where the state depends only on a single linear index or a fixed window of previous states (e.g., dp[i] depends on dp[i-1], dp[i-2]).
important_details: State transition usually looks backward by a fixed number of steps (1, 2, or k).
Highly optimizable to O(1) space using 2-3 variables instead of an entire array.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(N) -> O(1) optimized.

variations.description: Problems involving selecting items to maximize profit or achieve a target sum given weight/cost constraints. Includes 0/1 Knapsack (pick at most once) and Unbounded Knapsack (pick multiple times).
important_details: State: dp[i][w] represents the max value using the first 'i' items with capacity 'w'.
0/1 Knapsack Transition: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], val[i-1] + dp[i-1][w-wt[i-1]])
Space optimization requires iterating the capacity loop BACKWARDS for 0/1 Knapsack, and FORWARDS for Unbounded Knapsack.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N * W). Space Complexity: O(W).

problems.name: Number of Ways to Fill Knapsack

variations.description: DP applied to strings or arrays to find relationships like Longest Common Subsequence (LCS), Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS), or minimum edits to transform one string to another.
important_details: State: dp[i][j] represents the solution for string1[0..i-1] and string2[0..j-1].
LCS Transition: If match, dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]; else dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
LIS can be solved in O(N log N) using Binary Search (Patience Sorting) instead of O(N^2) DP.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(M * N). Often requires backtracking the DP table to reconstruct the actual string/subsequence.

variations.description: Used when a problem asks for the optimal way to merge, partition, or process a contiguous sequence of elements. The state represents a range [i, j].
important_details: State: dp[i][j] represents the optimal cost/value for the interval from index i to j.
Transition: Iterate a split point 'k' between i and j. dp[i][j] = min/max(dp[i][k] + dp[k+1][j] + cost(i, j, k)).
Iteration order: Gap/Length based. You must solve all smaller intervals of length L before solving intervals of length L+1.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N^3). Space Complexity: O(N^2). Common in Matrix Chain Multiplication and Burst Balloons.

variations.description: DP applied to 2D grids where the state depends on adjacent cells (usually top, left, or diagonal). Used for pathfinding or counting ways in a matrix.
important_details: State: dp[i][j] represents the optimal path or number of ways to reach cell (i, j).
Transition: dp[i][j] = derived from dp[i-1][j] and dp[i][j-1] for standard right/down traversal.
Obstacles or specific cell values modify the transition logic.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(M * N). Space Complexity: O(M * N) -> O(N) optimized using 1D array.

variations.description: DP where a state machine is used to track multiple conditions simultaneously (e.g., holding a stock, not holding a stock, cooldown period).
important_details: Define explicit states: e.g., State 0 (Hold), State 1 (Sold/Not Hold), State 2 (Cooldown).
Transitions map how you move from one state to another based on actions (buy, sell, rest).
Highly space-optimizable to O(1) by keeping only previous day's states.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(1). Always draw the state diagram first.

variations.description: Applying DP to tree structures where the state at a node depends on the states of its children. Usually implemented via Post-order DFS.
important_details: State: Typically returns an array/tuple of (include_node, exclude_node) or (max_path_through_node, max_path_anywhere).
Post-order traversal is mandatory: solve subproblems (left/right subtrees) before the current node.
Watch out for recursion depth limits; may require increasing stack size in JVM for extremely deep trees.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(H) where H is tree height (recursion stack).

variations.description: DP used when the state involves subsets of a small collection of items (usually N <= 20). A bitmask integer represents which items are used/visited.
important_details: State: dp[mask] where 'mask' is an integer whose bits represent included items (e.g., 1011 means items 0, 1, 3 are used).
Transition: Iterate over unset bits: new_mask = mask | (1 << i).
Only feasible for N <= 20 because space and time scale as 2^N.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(2^N * N^2). Space Complexity: O(2^N * N).

variations.description: Technique to count numbers in a range [L, R] that satisfy a specific property. It builds numbers digit by digit from left to right.
important_details: State: dp(pos, tight, leading_zero, state_properties).
tight: Boolean indicating if the prefix matches the upper bound exactly.
leading_zero: Boolean to handle cases where leading zeros shouldn't count as digits.
Answer for [L, R] is computed as solve(R) - solve(L-1).
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(log(R) * states). Used heavily in competitive programming for large bounds (up to 10^18).

problems.name: Numbers At Most N Given Digit Set

variations.description: Optimizing O(N^2) DP transitions to O(N log N) or O(N) by using data structures like Segment Trees, Binary Indexed Trees, Monotonic Queues, or Binary Search.
important_details: Transition looks like: dp[i] = min/max(dp[j] + cost(i, j)) for valid j < i.
If the cost function is separable and linear, Convex Hull Trick (CHT) or Li Chao Tree is used.
If finding max in a sliding window of states, Monotonic Queue is used.
variations.other_relevant_details: Crucial to identify the monotonicity or separability of the cost function to apply these optimizations.

variations.description: DP where the state transitions involve probabilities or expected values rather than deterministic costs.
important_details: State: dp(s) = probability of reaching target from state s, OR expected value/cost from state s.
Transition: dp(s) = Sum( P(s -> s') * dp(s') ) for all next states s'.
Base cases are usually 1.0 for success states and 0.0 for failure states.
variations.other_relevant_details: Beware of cyclic dependencies (e.g., dice games); may require solving systems of linear equations or iterative approximation.

problems.name: Probability of a Two Boxes Having The Same Number of Distinct Balls

variations.description: Dividing an array or sequence into K contiguous or non-contiguous partitions to minimize/maximize a specific cost function.
important_details: State: dp[i][k] = min/max cost to partition first 'i' elements into 'k' parts.
Transition: dp[i][k] = min/max(dp[j][k-1] + cost(j+1, i)) for j in range(0, i).
Requires a fast way to compute cost(j, i), often using prefix sums.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N^2 * K). Can be optimized using Divide and Conquer DP optimization or Knuth's optimization if the cost function satisfies the quadrangle inequality.

variations.description: Technique to compute for every mask the sum of values of all its submasks. Highly specific to bitwise subset calculations.
important_details: State: dp[mask][i] = sum of subsets of 'mask' differing only in the first 'i' bits.
Transition: If i-th bit is set, dp[mask][i] = dp[mask][i-1] + dp[mask ^ (1<<i)][i-1]. Else, dp[mask][i] = dp[mask][i-1].
Iterates over bits and masks, building the solution incrementally.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N * 2^N). Space Complexity: O(2^N). Widely used in combinatorics and bitwise CP problems.

problems.name: Minimum XOR Sum of Two Arrays

variations.description: DP involving 3 or more state variables, often used when tracking progress across multiple strings simultaneously or handling multi-constraint problems.
important_details: State: e.g., dp[i][j][k] where dimensions track string A, string B, and a constraint.
Careful initialization of 3D base cases is critical (usually zeros for i=0, j=0, or k=0).
Memory limits can be tight; optimize dimensions if any state is binary.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(L * M * N). Space Complexity: O(L * M * N). Can sometimes be optimized to O(M * N) using 2 layers.
